simple.meaning: מִקְלַעַת (miqlaʻath) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a sculpture (probably in bas-relief).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 6:18. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִקְלַעַת (H4734) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מִקְלַעַת (miqlaʻath) / H4734 is traced through 1 Kings 6:18, 1 Kings 6:29, 1 Kings 6:32, 1 Kings 7:31 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: There was cedar on the house within, carved with buds and open flowers. All was cedar. No stone was visible.

timeline.evidenceText: There was cedar on the house within, carved with buds and open flowers. All was cedar. No stone was visible.
He carved all the walls of the house around with carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, inside and outside.
So he made two doors of olive wood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold. He spread the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.

Its mouth within the capital and above was a cubit. Its mouth was round after the work of a pedestal, a cubit and a half; and also on its mouth were engravings, and their panels were square, not round.
